title: What people frame, iii
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: A child's drawing, framed by a father who says nothing. Wood says nothing back. A first.

panels.composition: The counter. A FATHER in a mill jacket — the mill's been closed six years — with a child's crayon drawing: a house, a dog, a very tall tree.
props: mill jacket with a faded logo

image.prompt: a quiet man in a faded mill jacket holding out a child's crayon drawing of a house, a dog and a very tall tree at a frame-shop counter

panels.composition: The drawing. The tree is taller than the house. The dog is bigger than the tree.

image.prompt: close-up of a child's crayon drawing where the tree is taller than the house and the dog is bigger than the tree

panels.composition: Wood opening his mouth. Closing it. Choosing a frame. Red. The father nods once.

characters.pose: holding up a red frame, saying nothing

image.prompt: a young man silently holding up a red frame to a man in a mill jacket who nods once, no words

panels.composition: The father gone. Wood at the counter, looking at the door. The pad open beside him. He doesn't draw this one.

characters.pose: looking at the door, pad open, pen down

image.prompt: a young man alone at a frame-shop counter looking at the door, an open blank drawing pad beside him with the pen set down, black and white, no words
image.notes: The first customer he doesn't draw. Note the blank pad.

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The first time Wood says nothing. The first customer he doesn't draw.
